dedupe_keys.name: high resolution lidar point clouds along the dalton highway alaska january 2024

description: This dataset gives high-resolution LiDAR point clouds collected along the Dalton Highway (Alaska Route 11), the remote road of about 414 miles from Livengood to Deadhorse near the Arctic Ocean that was built as a supply route for the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System and still serves the Prudhoe Bay oil fields. The survey was made on 10 January 2024 as part of efforts to provide geospatial data for cold-region research on the corridor, such as permafrost dynamics and thermokarst formation, and the package holds two merged point clouds in LAZ format (about 9.2 GB and 0.6 GB) with EML metadata. It was produced by researchers of the University of North Dakota and published in 2024 on the Defense Resiliency Platform Against Extreme Cold Weather, a DataONE member node. Coverage is a site-scale corridor segment between latitudes 65.49 and 65.88 degrees north. The files are public and free through DataONE; no licence is stated in the metadata. Caveats: only one winter date is covered, and the processing level and point density are not given on the record. The data support hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies of roads on permafrost and cold-region asset inspection, and relate to the US railroad climate hazard database catalogued here as another transport hazard resource.
